questions.question: What does the Lincoln index measure?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Population Size.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Lincoln Index **provides a way to measure the **population sizes** of **individual animal species.**
 
• It is based on a **capture /mark/recapture method.**
 
• The **Lincoln Index** is a method that is used to estimate the size of closed populations.
 
• Random samples of the population are captured and these individuals are marked and then released to mingle with the general population.
 
• The** population is resampled **after enough time has passed to allow** complete remixing of the marked individuals. **
 
• This will vary depending on the species, as well as its **habitat and mobility. **

questions.question: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was Dadabhai Naoroji the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta Session, 1886**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was a prominent Indian political leader who was elected President of the Indian National Congress (INC) during the Calcutta Session in 1886.
 
• His presidency marked a significant period in the Indian freedom struggle, emphasizing the need for greater autonomy and self-governance.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji is often referred to as the "**Grand Old Man of India**" for his contributions to Indian politics and his role in the independence movement.
 
• Under his leadership, the Congress session focused on issues like the economic exploitation of India by the British and the need for political reforms.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the **House of Commons in the UK**, furthering the cause of Indian independence on an international platform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• Founded in 1885, the INC was the first modern nationalist movement to emerge in the British Empire in Asia and Africa.
 
• The INC played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was instrumental in shaping the political discourse in India, advocating for self-rule and civil rights.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**
 
 
• Born on September 4, 1825, in Bombay (now Mumbai), he was a scholar, trader, and politician.
 
• He was a co-founder of the London Indian Society and the East India Association.
 
• His book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" highlighted the economic drain of India by the British.
 
 
 
• **Drain Theory**
 
 
• Proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, it suggested that a significant portion of India's wealth was being transferred to Britain, leading to widespread poverty in India.
 
• The theory emphasized the economic exploitation of India under British rule.
 
 
 
• **Congress Sessions**
 
 
• The annual sessions of the INC were significant events where leaders discussed strategies and policies for the independence movement.
 
• These sessions were platforms for addressing key issues such as economic policies, social reforms, and political strategies.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India lays down the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as 250?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Article 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 80** of the Constitution lays down the **maximum strength** of the **Rajya Sabha as 250.**
 
• Out of **250 seats** of the Rajya Sabha, **12 members are nominated by the President.**
 
• **238** are** representatives of the States** and of the two Union Territories.
 
• **Rajya Sabha **is the** Upper House of the Indian Parliament.**
 
• **Rajya Sabha** consists of the representatives of the States and the Union Territories and persons nominated by the President of India.
 
• **The Vice-President** of India is the **ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.**
 
• **Rajya Sabha **also chooses from amongst its Members, a **Deputy Chairman**.
 
• **Chairman, Rajya Sabha** and Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha **preside over its sittings.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 81** of the Indian Constitution defines the makeup of the House of the People, Lok Sabha.

 
 
• The House of Representatives shall have no more than 550 members elected, with little than 20 from Territories.
 
 
 
• **Article 83** Duration of Houses of Parliament.
 
 
• The Council of States shall not be subject to dissolution,
 
• but as nearly as possible one-third of the members thereof shall retire as soon as may be on the expiration of every second year following the provisions made in that behalf by Parliament by law.
 
 
 
• **Article 85** Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution.
 
 
• The President shall from time to time summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place
 
• As he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

questions.question: Which of the following terms is NOT related to the structure of a stupa?
questions.solution:
correct answer is__** ​Vimana.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Vimana is the structure over the** garbhagriha or inner sanctum in the Hindu temples of South India and Odisha in East India**.
 
• In typical temples of Odisha using the **Kalinga style** of architecture, the vimana is the **tallest structure of the temple**, as it is in the shikhara towers of temples in West and North India.
 
• By contrast, **in large South Indian temples**, it is typically** smaller than the great gatehouses or gopuram**, which are the most immediately striking architectural elements in a temple complex.
 
• A vimana is usually shaped as a** pyramid, consisting of several stories or tala**.
 
• Vimana are divided in two groups: **jati vimanas** that have up to four tala and **mukhya vimana** that have five tala and more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The stupa has **three special features **found in every stupa across the world.

 
 
• They are** A hemispherical mound (anda)**: The anda’s domed shape **(green highlights**) recalls a mound of dirt that was used to cover the Buddha’s remains.
 
• A **square railing (harmika)**: The harmika **(red highlights)** is inspired by a square railing or fence that surrounded the mound of dirt, marking it as a sacred burial site.
 
• A** central pillar** supporting a triple-umbrella form** (chattra)**: It was derived from umbrellas that were placed over the mound to protect it from the elements (purple highlights).

questions.question: Which of the following steps must be performed first in the classical Odissi dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangalacharan.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• "Mangalacharan" refers to the **opening piece or invocation performed** at the beginning of a dance recital or musical performance.
 
• The purpose of Mangalacharan is to invoke the blessings of the divine, seek auspiciousness.
 
• It often includes rhythmic footwork, expressive gestures, and melodic elements.
 
• Mangalacharan serves as a tribute to the gods and goddesses, as well as a way to express gratitude.

 
• **Important Mudras of classical Odissi dance**

 
 
• Pataka
 
• Ardhapataka
 
• Arala
 
• Suchi
 
• Shukachanchu
 
• Alapadma
 
• Ardha Chandra
 
• Kapitha
 
• Katakamukha
 
• Hansasya hastasPallava
 
• Keshabandha
 
• Karihasta
 
• Latarabya Nritta Hastas
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odissi dance form derives its name from the **Odra Nritya mentioned in the Natya Shastra.**
 
• This dance was primarily practised by the maharis and was patronised by **Kharavela**.
 
• **Guru Pankaj Charn Das** was a famous proponent of this dance.
 
• The earliest trace of this dance form was found in the **Udaygiri-Khandagiri caves in Odisha.**
 
• The variants of this dance form are **Gotipua and Nartala**, which is the court dance.
 
• The **Tribhanga **posture and mudras or hand gestures are the most important feature of Odissi.
 
• One of the popular themes of this dance form is the spiritual** love of Radha and Krishna.**

questions.question: The second session of Round Table Conference was held in:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1931**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Second Round Table Conference was held in London from 7 September 1931 to 1 December 1931 with the participation of Gandhi and the Indian National Congress.
 
• **Participants of the Second Round table conference**
 
 
• British delegates belonging to various political parties including the British Prime Minister, James Ramsay Macdonald.
 
• Indian princely states represented by Maharajas, princes and divans.
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)** – Mahatma Gandhi, Rangaswami Iyengar, Madan Mohan Malaviya
 
• **Muslims** – Md. Ali Jinnah, Aga Khan III, Muhammad Iqbal, etc.
 
• **Hindus** – M R Jayakar, etc.
 
• **Depressed classes** – Dr B R Ambedkar
 
• **Women** – Sarojini Naidu, etc.
 
• Liberals, Justice Party, Sikhs, Indian Christians, Parsis, Europeans, Anglo-Indians, industry, labour, landlords, Burma, Sindh and other provinces.
 
 
 
• **Outcome of Second Round Table Conference**
 
 
• The major difference between the first and the second conference was that the INC was participating in the second one. This was one of the results of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
 
• The British decided to** grant a communal award** for representing minorities in India by providing for separate electorates for minority communities. Gandhi was against this.
 
• In this conference, **Gandhi and Ambedkar differed** on the issue of separate electorates for the untouchables. Gandhi was against treating untouchables as separate from the Hindu community. This issue was resolved through the **Poona Pact 1932**.
 
• The second round table conference was deemed a failure because of the many disagreements among the participants. While the INC claimed to speak for the whole of the country, other participants and leaders of other parties contested this claim.

questions.question: Which cell organelle containing millions of membrane-bound ribosomes is involved in the production, folding, quality control and dispatch of certain proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rough endoplasmic reticulum**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The Endoplasmic reticulum is composed of the following **three kinds of structures**:

 
 
• **Cisternae **which occur in those cells which have synthetic roles,
 
• **Tubules **that are involved in lipid and sterol synthesis and
 
• **Vesicles **that are membrane-bound vacuolar structures.
 
 
 
• The Endoplasmic Reticulum of **two types:**
 
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum** consists mainly of tubules and vesicles.
 
• Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum is involved in fat and steroidal hormone.
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum** consists of cisternae, it has ribosomes attached to its cytoplasmic surface.
 
• The Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum provides a surface for protein synthesis.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Golgi Apparatus** is a cell organelle that **processes the proteins and lipid molecules** and

 
 
• proteins that are destined to be exported from the cell.
 
• It is a part of the cell that is made up of membranes and some of them are tubules and nuclei.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria** is a **membrane-bound cell organelle** which generates most of the chemical energy required for the cell.
 
 
• It is also called as **powerhouse of the cell**

questions.question: What was the minimum consumption expenditure (₹ per capita per month) set as a benchmark of the poverty line for rural India in 1979?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**49.09**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Poverty line benchmark for **rural India in 1979**: **₹49 per capita per month**.
 
• Used by the **Planning Commission **to gauge **poverty rates and design policies**.
 
• Based on essential expenses for **food, clothing, and housing**.
 
• Guided development of **poverty alleviation programs**.
 
• Reviewed periodically to adjust for **economic changes**.
 
• Recognized variations in living **conditions among households**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MGNREGA** was implemented in** 2006** to address poverty through **rural employment**.

 
 
• Provides **100 days of wage employment per year **to rural households.
 
• Aims to enhance **livelihood security and create rural assets**.
 
• Contributes to **poverty reduction and social inclusion**.
 
• Faces challenges like **delays in wage payments **and **administrative inefficiencies**.
 
• Ongoing efforts to **strengthen implementation and effectiveness**.
 
 
 
• The **Public Distribution System **(PDS), ongoing since the **1940s**, provides **subsidised food to vulnerable populations to alleviate poverty**.

questions.question: In which year did Rajpath become the permanent venue for the Republic Day parade?

__
 
• The parade takes place every year on Republic day (26th of January) at Rajpath in New Delhi.
 
• Rajpath become the permanent venue for the Republic Day parade in 1955.
 
• The parade is being organised by the **Ministry of **Defence.
 
• The parade showcases a multi-hued image of the country's rich cultural heritage and military power.
 
• This parade is presided over by the President of India.
 
• The first Republic Day parade was held in 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It symbolises a shift from erstwhile Rajpath being an icon of power, to** Kartavya Path being an example of public ownership and empowerment**
